name: Matrixyl

lead: Matrixyl (palmitoyl pentapeptide-4, Pal-KTTKS) is a lipid-modified fragment of type I procollagen developed by a cosmetic ingredient supplier for anti-wrinkle products. It appears in many serums and eye creams.
Supporting data are mainly from supplier-sponsored or small studies, so independent evidence of visible improvement is limited.

paras: The peptide is thought to mimic collagen breakdown fragments that signal fibroblasts to make new collagen and other matrix components. The palmitoyl group is added to help it cross the skin barrier.
It is considered low-risk, with rare irritation, and is freely sold as a cosmetic. Effects are modest and benefits depend on formulation and the concentration achieved at the target layer.
